DST repeated delivery is not proven by future next-time metadata.
General Cloud Scheduler resource API is not claimed.
The Fireemu-only conditions are bound to local tests and claim no production behaviour.

A snapshot restore that is rolled back because a later hook refuses it resets the functions runtime a second time: the schedule queue from before the restore is discarded and every schedule cursor stays at the restored time, so occurrences can repeat or be skipped. Known; not fixed here.

With scheduler.catchUp all and scheduler.overlap skip or reject, one clock move over several occurrences of a function overlaps itself (skip keeps the oldest, reject counts the rest). The behaviour is pinned by a test, not endorsed.
scheduler.clock wall is declared in the config schema and refused at load as not implemented.

overlap-policy is verified by the frozen local cases and the W3 supplemental rows on the final artifact inputs. Legacy skip and reject count queued, running and retry-waiting runs as busy. Strict defaults to skip-in-flight, which counts only a running handler of the same function, admits manual runs and does not count queued occurrences of one sweep. Production Scheduler-attempt versus handler-instance boundaries remain undetermined under ruling 3.3.

After a rewind below a schedule cursor that trails the clock (a catchUp all backlog that was cut at the cap, or a run held for room), the owed runs stay owed but do not come due again until the clock passes the cursor, and the session reports idle meanwhile. Documented in the README; no test pins it.

scheduler.defaultTimeZone is tested only for a configured value (it moves the occurrences of a schedule that names no zone). What a schedule that names no zone and has no configured default does is not claimed: firebase-tools deploys a zone-less v1 schedule as America/Los_Angeles, and run 4 confirms that CLI default. Final-artifact omitted-zone interval receipts and the loaded v1 manifest now confirm the calendar behavior and effective CLI default.

The token response shapes asserted after a rewind (INVALID_ID_TOKEN, the Storage 401 and the Firestore PermissionDenied in strict, TOKEN_EXPIRED for a sign-in below the account creation) are inferred from the ID-token contract by owner ledger 781 and scope decision S8. A rewound clock has no production counterpart, so they are local rulings, not production parity; AUTH-CREDENTIAL owns them.
